newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania q1 budget gap said at 1.98 trillion lei.
newsitem.headline: Romania q1 budget gap said at 1.98 trillion lei.

text.p: Romania's state budget gap was 1.98 trillion lei at the end of the first quarter of 1997, or 16 percent of the forecast whole-year deficit, due to cautious spending, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Tuesday.

"In the period since (the government) came to office, the fiscal and budget policy has been characterised by austerity which, parallelled by a restrictive monetary policy, diminished price adjustment shocks," Ciorbea told a news conference.
His remarks were made in a state-of-the-nation analysis of economic reform progress in the almost six months since his centrist cabinet replaced leftists in elections.
Ciorbea said that, at the end of the first quarter, the consolidated budget posted a deficit of 2.35 trillion lei, or 22.5 percent of the gap forecast for the whole year.
The consolidated budget includes the state budget, local government budgets, social security budget, supplementary pension funds and various other extra-budgetary funds.
"This deficit was financed through non-inflationary sources," Ciorbea said.

Under the 1997 budget -- agreed with international lenders and approved by parliament in April -- the state budget gap was set at 12.6 trillion lei, or 5.4 percent, of the gross domestic product. The consolidated budget deficit was trimmed to 4.5 percent of the GDP, against 5.8 percent in 1996.
Ciorbea recently said the 1997 budget gap would be financed through external credits -- about 3.4 percent -- with the rest funded by domestic loans.
Romania last month got the first $86 million tranche of a $430 million loan from the International Monetary Fund. The World Bank also pledged $630 million in credits.
According to latest estimates, Romania would end the year with 12-month inflation of 110 percent, up from a previous forecast of around 90 percent.
